segments.narration: Birds crashing into Lake Natron get calcified into stone mummies. Photographers found perfectly preserved bats and songbirds lining the shoreline.
The hyper-reflective water acts like an optical trap, luring flying animals to crash straight into the chemical bath.
So what turns soft feathers and flesh into solid rock? Water temperatures reach 140 degrees, with alkalinity rivaling pure ammonia.
Surrounding volcanoes leak massive amounts of natron, a sodium compound that rapidly coats drowned animals in a calcified mineral crust.
It is the exact salt ancient Egyptians used for mummification, making this lake a natural factory of living statues.
